To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
62.5% of HHT patients carry a germline mutation in one of the two known HHT genes, ENG and ALK.
we have identified a total of 100 mutations in the ENG and ALK-1 genes in 100 unrelated French patients with hereditary hemorrhagic teleangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome).
the majority of patients with HHT have a germline mutation in either the ENG or the ALK1 genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of mutations in ENG and ALK in a large cohort of HHT patients in France, with a high rate of mutation detection.
the identification of new mutations in the two HHT genes and the analysis of their distribution.
the molecular screening of ALK and ENG genes in HHT patients in France, which provides a comprehensive analysis of mutations in both genes and a useful resource for clinical diagnosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HHT in French patients is mainly caused by ENG and ALK mutations, which are frequently novel.
62.5% of French HHT patients have a mutation in one of the two HHT genes, with a higher frequency of mutations in ALK 1 (40.6%) than in ENG (21.9%), and that 33.1% of the mutations were recurrent.
62.5% of the index cases in this series had a germline mutation in one of the two genes, with a higher proportion in the ENG gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of HHT families in France have a mutation in one of the two genes, with the majority of mutations in ALK 1.
100/160 unrelated French index patients were found to have a mutation in either ENG or ALK1 genes and that 36 ENG and 64 ALK1 mutations were found, 33 ENG and 27 ALK1 of them being novel mutations.
the most frequent mutation in HHT patients is c.1112dupG in ALK1 gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
molecular diagnosis is possible for most of the patients and that the genetic screening of both ENG and ALK 1 is necessary to identify mutations in HHT.
molecular screening of ENG and ALC1 is a useful approach for the diagnosis of HHT, even in the absence of family history.

molecular analysis of the ALK1/ENG genes is now a reliable and useful tool for HHT diagnosis, and that the identification of recurrent mutations in ALKS1/ENG genes could help to better understand the genetic basis of this disease and to improve genetic counseling.
